observation.description: The natural deploy-shaped evolution workflow — stop the dev server, regenerate the evolved schema/functions, start again over the same database — refuses on a sessions app with SNAPBACK_AUTH_STARTUP_ARTIFACT_MISMATCH ('startup artifact pair differs from the pinned deployment'), and the CLI then wraps that cause in SNAPBACK_RUNTIME_ARTIFACT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH, telling the consumer the runtime 'could not deserialize artifacts emitted by the current codegen' and advising a runtime reinstall/rebuild or a SNAPBACK_RUNTIME_BINARY override. The actual cause (the auth-mode startup pin) appears only in a stderr line; the structured diagnostic names the wrong subsystem and the recovery advice cannot help. An external consumer who followed it would reinstall packages in a loop.
evidence: demos/improvement-sweep/arms/a3-snapback-web/evidence/app/repro-evolution.mjs (probe: v1 boot, stop, v2 regenerate, boot refused with the cascade)

competitorOutcome.description: Convex's push-based evolution has no equivalent restart pin: 'npx convex dev' pushes the evolved schema to the running deployment and errors name the schema conflict itself (frozen Linear-arm evidence exercised a production-shaped schema change without a misattributed failure).

mustNotRegress: The startup pin itself — a sessions deployment must keep refusing to silently adopt a different artifact pair at boot; fail-closed stays.
smallestCoherentFix: Propagate the true cause: when dev-server start fails with an auth-subsystem code, surface THAT code as the primary structured diagnostic with a recovery naming the sanctioned evolution path (live reload through the running supervisor, or an explicit artifact-pair admission step), and reserve RUNTIME_ARTIFACT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH for genuine deserialization failures.
acceptanceWitness: The stop/regenerate/start sequence on a sessions database emits SNAPBACK_AUTH_STARTUP_ARTIFACT_MISMATCH as the primary structured diagnostic with a recovery pointing at the supported evolution step, and that step then succeeds.
